plainContent: The Ant and the Grasshopper Throughout the warm months, an ant carried grains to a dry store beneath a tree. Nearby, a grasshopper spent the days singing and resting in the sun. The ant invited him to gather food before winter, but the grasshopper replied that there was plenty of time. The ant continued working a little every day. He did not refuse rest or happiness; he simply prepared before the weather changed. Soon cold rain covered the fields, insects disappeared, and the grasshopper found nothing to eat. Hungry and shivering, he went to the ant’s shelter and asked for help. The ant shared a small meal but explained that kindness could not replace planning. He advised the grasshopper to gather food whenever spring returned and to balance enjoyment with responsibility. The grasshopper understood that he had confused leisure with a life without duties. When warm weather came again, he worked beside the ant each morning and sang only after storing enough food. The two friends remained helpful to one another. Moral: Prepare during good times, and do not sacrifice necessary work for immediate pleasure.

title: The Justice of Quazi Completing Story

plainContent: The Justice of Quazi Sultan Giasuddin Azam was known as a ruler who expected even powerful people to obey the law. One day, while hunting, he accidentally shot a young boy instead of the deer he had aimed at. The boy died, leaving his widowed mother in deep grief. The mother brought her complaint before the Sultan. Although he was the ruler, Giasuddin did not use his position to silence her. He asked the respected Quazi to hear the case. The Quazi examined the witnesses and announced that the Sultan was responsible for the death and must face the same law as any other citizen. The Sultan accepted the judgment without anger. He prepared to receive the punishment, but the grieving mother saw that the ruler had admitted his responsibility and respected the court. She forgave him, saying that a king who submits to justice should not be treated as a deliberate murderer. The story shows that justice loses its meaning when rank places someone above the law. A fair ruler earns trust by accepting accountability, even when the decision is painful.

title: A Journey by Bus Composition

plainContent: Across the countryside by road During the winter vacation, I travelled by bus from our town to visit my aunt. We reached the terminal early, bought our tickets, and found seats beside a window. After leaving the crowded streets, the bus passed fields, ponds, markets, and small settlements. The road was lively. Farmers carried produce, schoolchildren waited at stops, and rickshaws moved carefully through the villages. At a roadside café we took a short break and drank water. A brief traffic jam delayed us, but the driver remained careful and patient rather than speeding. The view changed as we approached the destination: green farmland gave way to busier shops and buildings. Although the seats were not very comfortable, the trip was enjoyable because I observed ordinary life beyond my neighbourhood. We arrived safely before sunset, and the warm welcome from my aunt made the long ride worthwhile.

plainContent: The visitor who valued kindness One night, Abu Ben Adhem awoke and saw a gentle figure writing in a golden book. He asked whether his name had been recorded among those who loved God. The figure replied that it had not, so Abu quietly returned to sleep. The next evening the visitor appeared again. Abu asked what was being written. This time he saw his name listed among people who loved their fellow human beings. He was pleased, because he had always tried to help the poor, comfort the troubled, and treat neighbours with respect. The following morning the book showed the names of those especially favoured by God, and Abu’s name stood at the top. He understood that sincere service to people is a powerful form of worship. Goodness is proved not by proud words but by compassionate actions. Moral: Love for humanity is a true sign of devotion.

plainContent: A frightening event on a busy road One afternoon I saw a collision near a crowded crossing. A motorcycle tried to pass a bus while a pedestrian was crossing the road. The sudden movement caused a crash, and the rider fell while the pedestrian suffered a minor injury. People gathered, but a few tried to move the injured person carelessly. A responsible shopkeeper asked everyone to make space, called emergency services, and noted the vehicle number. Another person directed traffic until help arrived. The incident showed that curiosity must never be more important than safety. Road accidents often result from speeding, careless overtaking, distracted driving, weak enforcement, or unsafe crossings. Drivers should obey signals, wear helmets or seat belts, and never use a phone while moving. Pedestrians should use marked crossings and remain alert. Roads become safer when authorities provide good design and every traveller accepts personal responsibility.

title: Deforestation Composition
excerpt: Deforestation Composition: We write Deforestation Composition with an easy and advanced variant, which is suitable for classes 6,7,8,10, SSC, and […]
plainContent: Forests and the danger of losing them Deforestation is the removal of trees over a large area without allowing the forest to recover. People clear land for farms, roads, settlements, fuel, and commercial timber. Illegal cutting and weak management make the loss even faster. Forests protect soil, hold water, moderate temperature, and provide homes for countless plants and animals. They also absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen. When trees disappear, hills erode, rivers become silted, rainfall patterns may change, and wildlife loses its habitat. Communities may then face floods, droughts, hotter weather, and shortages of forest products. Stopping deforestation requires more than planting a few saplings. Existing forests must be guarded, illegal logging must be punished, and local people should receive legal ways to earn a living without destroying trees. Reforestation projects should use suitable native species and care for them until they are established. Every citizen can help by using paper carefully, planting trees, supporting responsible products, and reporting destructive activities. Forest conservation protects both nature and human life, so it deserves continuous attention rather than occasional campaigns.

title: There was a pond full of Frogs Story

plainContent: The Pond of Frogs A group of children discovered a pond where frogs lived. The frogs spent their days swimming, calling, and resting among the water plants. The children thought it amusing to throw pebbles whenever a frog appeared above the surface. At first the children laughed at their game. The frogs, however, were frightened and injured. Some dived desperately, while others were struck by stones. An old frog finally called from the water, “Your game is our danger. Please stop.” The children looked more carefully and saw that several frogs were hurt. They had never imagined that their amusement could cause pain to another living creature. Feeling ashamed, they put down the stones and went to tell their teacher what had happened. The teacher explained that people should consider the effect of an action, even when it seems small or entertaining. The children promised to protect the pond. They cleared rubbish from its edge and watched the frogs without disturbing them. Later they taught younger children the same lesson. Moral: We must not make fun or entertainment from another creature’s suffering.

plainContent: A peaceful trip on the river Last autumn I travelled by boat from our town to my uncle’s riverside village. We boarded before sunrise with a small bag of food and watched the mist slowly lift from the water. As the boat moved forward, fishermen pulled in their nets and village boats crossed our route. The riverbank offered a changing view: green fields, bamboo clusters, grazing cattle, and children waving from sandy steps. The boatman guided us around bends while the current made a soft, steady sound. At midday we shared lunch under a cloth canopy and stopped briefly near a market to buy fresh fruit. The journey took longer than a road trip, but its quiet rhythm made it memorable. I saw how closely many families depend on the river for travel, fishing, and farming. When we reached the village in the afternoon, I felt refreshed and grateful for the simple beauty of the trip.

title: The King and the Astrologer story

plainContent: The King and the Astrologer A king once invited an astrologer to tell him what the future held. The visitor gave an answer that displeased him, and the angry king ordered that the man be punished. Before the guards led him away, the king asked how long he himself would live. The astrologer paused and replied calmly, “Your Majesty, I am certain that I shall die only a short time before you.” The king was startled. If the astrologer died first, he feared that people might suspect the king had caused it. He immediately cancelled the punishment and ordered the man to leave safely. The astrologer’s quick answer had saved his life, but the king later realised how dangerous his anger had been. A ruler who punishes people merely for speaking an unwelcome opinion cannot govern wisely. He decided to listen more patiently and to seek evidence before making decisions. The tale is not a lesson in predicting the future. It is a reminder that presence of mind can protect a person in danger and that authority must be guided by self-control. Anger often creates a problem that calm thought can prevent.

title: Patriotism Composition

plainContent: Patriotism Patriotism is sincere love for one’s country and a willingness to work for its welfare. It is more than loud slogans or emotional speeches. A patriotic person respects the nation’s history, values its people, and accepts a duty to improve public life. During Bangladesh’s Liberation War, countless people sacrificed their safety and lives for freedom. Remembering them should inspire citizens to be honest, disciplined, and helpful. A student shows patriotism by studying seriously, protecting public property, obeying rules, helping classmates, and learning the truth about the country’s past. An adult may show it by paying lawful taxes, doing a job responsibly, voting thoughtfully, and serving neighbours during a disaster. Patriotism must not become hatred of other nations or communities. True love of country includes respect for human dignity, minority rights, and peaceful cooperation with other peoples. It also requires the courage to identify corruption, pollution, injustice, and inequality instead of hiding them. If citizens combine affection with responsibility, Bangladesh can become stronger. The best patriot is not the person who merely claims to love the country, but the person whose daily conduct makes the country safer, fairer, and more prosperous.

title: Six Seasons of Bangladesh Composition

plainContent: Six Seasons of Bangladesh Bangladesh is traditionally described as a country of six seasons, each lasting about two Bengali months. Their changing temperatures, rainfall, crops, flowers, and festivals give the country a varied natural rhythm. Summer: Boishakh and Jyaishtha bring intense heat, occasional thunderstorms, and delicious mangoes, jackfruits, and lichis. People seek shade and drink plenty of water. Rainy season: Ashar and Shravan fill rivers, ponds, and fields. Rain supports farming, but floods and waterlogging may cause suffering. Autumn: Bhadra and Ashwin often offer clear blue skies, white clouds, and blooming kash flowers after the wet months. Late autumn: Kartik and Agrahayan bring cooler, drier weather and the harvesting of paddy. Rural life becomes busy with new grain. Winter: Poush and Magh are cool and sometimes foggy. Warm clothes, date-palm juice, vegetables, and village fairs are associated with this season. Spring: Falgun and Chaitra are mild and colourful. Trees produce new leaves and flowers, and the air feels lively before summer returns. This seasonal variety enriches agriculture, culture, and everyday life, although climate change is altering familiar patterns.

title: Female Education Composition

plainContent: Education for girls and women Female education means giving girls and women equal access to learning, skills, and the chance to use their knowledge. An educated woman can make informed decisions about health, finances, family, and civic life. She is also better prepared to earn an income and support others. When girls stay in school, child marriage and early motherhood often decline, while children in the next generation are more likely to receive care and education. Society gains teachers, doctors, entrepreneurs, researchers, and leaders whose abilities would otherwise remain unused. Barriers include poverty, unsafe travel, household expectations, inadequate facilities, and harmful beliefs that a girl’s education has little value. Scholarships, safe schools, sanitation facilities, supportive families, and strict action against harassment can remove these barriers. Educating women is not a favour to one group; it is an investment in the whole country. Equal education creates healthier families, stronger economies, and a more just society.

title: Padma Bridge paragraph for Class 6,7,8,SSC,HSC
excerpt: Padma Bridge paragraph: Dear students, brothers and sisters of class 6-12, today our topic of discussion is a paragraph on […]
plainContent: Padma Bridge The Padma Multipurpose Bridge is one of Bangladesh’s most important transport projects. It crosses the broad Padma River and links Louhajong in Munshiganj with areas of Shariatpur and Madaripur. In this way it gives the southwest a direct connection with Dhaka and the northern and eastern parts of the country. Construction began in 2014, and the bridge was opened by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on 25 June 2022. It is about 6.15 kilometres long and has two levels: the upper deck carries a four-lane road, while the lower deck is designed for a single railway track. Forty-two piers support forty-one steel spans. The project was financed from Bangladesh’s own public resources and built by China Major Bridge Engineering Company. The bridge has reduced dependence on ferries and made travel more predictable. Farmers can send products to markets more quickly, businesses can move goods efficiently, and people in the connected districts can reach hospitals, schools, and workplaces with greater ease. Its value is not only structural; it represents engineering confidence and a long-term investment in regional development.

title: A Village Doctor paragraph Easy word (100-250 words)
excerpt: A Village Doctor paragraph for classes 6,7,8, SSC, HSC: A village doctor is a very important person for every village’s […]
plainContent: A trusted health worker in a rural community A village doctor provides basic medical advice and treatment where a large hospital may be far away. People often consult this doctor for fever, minor injuries, common infections, first aid, and guidance about when specialist care is necessary. Because the doctor knows local families, patients may feel comfortable discussing their problems. A responsible village doctor must examine patients carefully, use medicines safely, keep records, and refer serious cases instead of pretending to treat everything. Vaccination, clean water, sanitation, nutrition, and maternal care are also important parts of community health. No doctor should sell unnecessary antibiotics or ignore warning signs. Rural clinics need trained staff, essential supplies, reliable electricity, transport links, and communication with hospitals. Villagers should follow prescriptions, avoid self-medication, and seek urgent help for severe symptoms. A capable village doctor can save time and lives, but good healthcare depends on a wider support system.

title: A Moonlit Night Paragraph for Class 6,7,8,SSC,HSC

plainContent: A quiet landscape under the moon A moonlit night is a night when the moon spreads a gentle brightness over the earth. The sky appears deep and clear, and stars can be seen between passing clouds. Trees, rooftops, ponds, and open fields take on soft shapes instead of their usual daytime colours. On such a night, the air often feels cooler and the surroundings become calm. The moon’s reflection trembles on water, while crickets and night birds provide a delicate natural song. People may sit outdoors, walk along a safe path, or simply look through a window and enjoy the peaceful scene. A moonlit night can refresh a tired mind and inspire poets, painters, and thoughtful observers. Yet rural travellers should still carry a light, because beautiful surroundings do not remove practical dangers. The quiet combination of light, shadow, and silence makes the experience one of nature’s most memorable gifts.

title: Computer Composition
excerpt: Computer Composition for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC, HSC: Here you will find a short composition on the computer explained […]
plainContent: The computer as a modern tool A computer is an electronic machine that accepts information, processes it, and produces useful results. It can perform calculations, store records, prepare documents, display pictures, and communicate with other devices in a very short time. Computers have changed education, medicine, business, agriculture, and public administration. Students use them to research lessons, prepare presentations, and practise skills. Doctors store patient information and examine digital reports. Offices manage accounts and communication more efficiently, while farmers can learn about weather and markets through online services. The internet makes a computer even more useful, but it also demands care. False information, unsafe websites, excessive gaming, and theft of personal data can harm users. A responsible person checks sources, protects passwords, limits screen time, and treats other people respectfully online. Computers are neither automatically good nor bad; their value depends on how people use them. Basic digital literacy should be taught widely so that technology improves work and learning instead of replacing judgement and human responsibility.

title: Uses and Abuses of Television Composition
excerpt: Television Composition for classes 6, 7, 8, SSC, HSC: Hello students, need a composition about the uses and abuses of […]
plainContent: Television: Uses and Abuses Television is an electronic medium that combines moving pictures and sound. It brings news, educational programmes, documentaries, drama, sport, music, and cultural events into the home. Families can learn about distant countries, health, science, history, and current affairs without travelling. Well-designed programmes can support classroom lessons and provide wholesome recreation. Television is useful when viewers choose programmes carefully and limit their screen time. It can help people relax after work and make important public messages reach a large audience quickly. During emergencies, broadcasts may provide warnings and instructions. However, excessive or careless viewing has disadvantages. Long hours of sitting can reduce exercise and sleep. Children may neglect homework, reading, family conversation, or outdoor play. Violent or misleading programmes can influence behaviour, and advertisements may encourage unnecessary consumption. Some viewers also accept a dramatic presentation as if it were verified news. Parents and students should make a sensible schedule, keep screens away during meals and study, and discuss what they watch. Television is neither wholly good nor wholly bad. Its value depends on the quality of its content and the wisdom with which it is used.

title: Internet Paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC | 100-250 words

plainContent: The Internet The internet connects millions of devices and enables people to share information across great distances. At home or school, a learner can search for explanations, read digital books, watch a lesson, submit work, or speak with a teacher. Families use it for communication, shopping, banking, entertainment, and work. Users must remember that not everything online is true or safe. We should compare reliable sources, use strong passwords, keep accounts private, and never harass another person. Spending too much time online can also damage sleep and study habits. A balanced routine and thoughtful behavior make the internet beneficial. It should support education and real relationships rather than replace careful thinking or direct human contact.

plainContent: Our National Flag A national flag gives a country a visible sign of identity and independence. Bangladesh’s flag is a green rectangle carrying a red circle slightly toward the hoist. The green recalls the country’s fertile land and lively natural landscape. The red suggests the rising sun as well as the sacrifice made during the struggle for freedom. The flag was designed by artist Kamrul Hassan in its present form. An earlier wartime design included a map of Bangladesh, but the map was later removed so that the flag would remain clear and easy to reproduce. The first version was raised publicly at the University of Dhaka on 2 March 1971, before independence was achieved. The proportions of the flag are 10 units in length to 6 units in width. It is flown on Independence Day, Victory Day, national ceremonies, schools, government buildings, and international occasions. Students should handle it carefully, keep it clean, and never allow it to touch the ground. Respect for the flag is respect for the people and history it represents.

title: Unemployment Problem in Bangladesh Composition
excerpt: Unemployment Problem in Bangladesh Composition for Classes 6,7,8,9,10, SSC, HSC: Here is a composition on the unemployment problem in Bangladesh […]
plainContent: Unemployment Problem in Bangladesh Unemployment means that people who are able and willing to work cannot find suitable paid work. Bangladesh has many young people entering the labour market, but opportunities do not always grow quickly enough. Educated graduates may lack practical skills, while rural workers can lose jobs during seasonal or economic difficulties. Several factors contribute to the problem: population growth, limited industrial expansion, weak career guidance, mismatch between education and employers’ needs, dependence on public-sector jobs, and unequal access to training and finance. Long-term unemployment causes poverty, frustration, migration, family pressure, and sometimes crime. Underemployment, in which a person works fewer hours or far below their ability, is also serious. Solutions include improving school quality, expanding technical and vocational education, supporting entrepreneurship, developing agriculture and small industries, and creating safe opportunities for women and people with disabilities. Transparent recruitment and investment outside the largest cities can spread employment more fairly. Young people can build skills in communication, technology, and trades while seeking work. Government, businesses, educators, and communities must cooperate. Productive citizens are an asset, so employment policy should focus on skills, dignity, and sustainable opportunities.

title: The Rainy Season in Bangladesh Composition

plainContent: The Rainy Season in Bangladesh Bangladesh experiences six seasons, and the rainy season is generally associated with Ashar and Shravan, the third and fourth months of the Bengali calendar. In practice, rain may continue into later months. Dark clouds gather, warm air cools, and showers can arrive suddenly after a long humid spell. Rain fills rivers, canals, ponds, and fields. Farmers welcome it because paddy and many other crops need water. Trees look fresh, fish move through flooded waterways, and the countryside becomes green. Children often enjoy paper boats and the sound of rain on roofs. The season also creates hardship. Excessive rain causes floods, waterlogging, erosion, transport disruption, and damage to homes and crops. People in low-lying areas may need shelters, clean drinking water, and medical assistance. Lightning and unsafe travel are additional dangers. Good drainage, raised roads, embankments, early warnings, and careful flood preparation reduce these risks. We should keep drains free of rubbish and avoid walking or travelling through fast-moving water. Thus the rainy season is both a blessing for agriculture and a test of preparedness for the people of Bangladesh.

title: Tree Plantation Composition

plainContent: Tree Plantation Trees support life in many ways. They absorb carbon dioxide, release oxygen, hold soil together, provide shade, reduce heat, shelter wildlife, and help regulate rainfall. Fruits, timber, fuel, medicines, and other materials also come from trees. Forests protect rivers and coastlines and contribute to the economy. Bangladesh has a dense population and limited land, so protecting existing trees and planting suitable new ones are both important. Planting beside roads, around schools, along canals, in courtyards, and on unused public land can increase green cover. Native species should be chosen for local soil and weather. A sapling is not enough: it must be watered, protected from animals, and cared for until it becomes established. Unplanned cutting, fires, pollution, and construction destroy vegetation. Laws against illegal felling should be enforced, while communities can organise seasonal planting and monitoring. Students can grow seedlings and teach others why trees matter. Tree plantation is most successful when it is followed by long-term care. Protecting a mature tree is often as valuable as planting a new one.

title: Rivers of Bangladesh Composition
excerpt: Rivers of Bangladesh Composition for Class 6, 7, 8, 10, SSC, HSC: In this post, you will find a composition […]
plainContent: Rivers of Bangladesh Rivers are central to the geography, economy, and culture of Bangladesh. The Padma, Jamuna, Meghna, and their many branches carry water and silt across the delta before reaching the Bay of Bengal. Countless smaller rivers, canals, and wetlands connect villages and support a rich variety of life. Rivers make the soil fertile and help farmers grow rice, jute, vegetables, and other crops. They provide fish, transport routes, irrigation, and water for households and industry. Riverbanks are also places of trade, work, songs, and festivals. In the rainy season many waterways swell and make the countryside beautiful. Yet rivers can cause erosion and floods, especially when heavy rain combines with upstream water. Pollution from sewage, plastic, oil, and untreated industrial waste threatens people and aquatic animals. Encroachment and careless sand extraction damage natural flow. Protecting rivers requires sewage treatment, responsible waste disposal, enforcement against illegal occupation, safe dredging, and careful flood planning. Communities should not throw rubbish into water. A clean, living river system is essential for food security, transport, biodiversity, and the future of Bangladesh.

title: Climate Change Composition
excerpt: Climate Change Composition: Climate Change Composition for HSC, SSC with 200, 250 Words variant. This composition on Climate Change is […]
plainContent: Why the climate is changing Climate change means a long-term shift in temperature, rainfall, seasons, and other patterns of weather. The natural climate has always changed gradually, but human activity has accelerated the process. Burning coal, oil, and gas releases carbon dioxide, while forests are cleared that would otherwise absorb part of it. The extra gases form a thicker heat-trapping layer around Earth. As a result, average temperatures rise and glaciers melt. Seas expand, storms may become stronger, and unusual floods, droughts, or heat waves occur more often. Bangladesh faces special risks because its low-lying delta is exposed to river floods, cyclones, salinity, and the loss of farmland. Solving the problem requires action at many levels. Governments can expand renewable energy, improve public transport, protect forests, and enforce environmental rules. Industries should reduce waste and use cleaner technology. Families can save electricity, avoid unnecessary plastic, plant trees, and choose shared transport when possible. Adaptation is necessary as well. Stronger shelters, early warnings, salt-tolerant crops, and careful water management can protect communities. Climate change is a global problem, but responsible choices made locally can help create a safer future.

Mothers who have received education are more likely to value vaccination, nutrition, and schooling for their children. Yet poverty, unsafe travel, early marriage, and social prejudice still prevent many girls from continuing their studies. Families, schools, and government should work together to remove these obstacles. Supporting female education creates opportunity, reduces inequality, and strengthens society.

plainContent: Rejecting dowry in marriage The dowry system demands money, goods, or property from a bride’s family before or after marriage. It places an unfair burden on parents and turns a relationship based on respect into a financial transaction. Families may borrow heavily or sell land to meet a demand. If they cannot pay, the bride may face insults, violence, or abandonment. Young women are treated as liabilities, and education may be neglected while relatives save for marriage expenses. These harms affect the whole community. The solution requires law enforcement, public awareness, and a change in social thinking. Families should refuse unlawful demands, support victims, and report abuse. Schools can teach that a person’s character and abilities matter more than wealth. Young men and women should promise that marriage will not be used to extract money. A dignified marriage needs consent, equality, and mutual responsibility. Ending dowry will protect families and strengthen the respect owed to women.

plainContent: Keeping the environment clean Air, water, and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic, and other waste are released carelessly. Polluted surroundings can cause illness, kill fish and plants, reduce soil fertility, and make cities uncomfortable to live in. Factories and vehicles should use cleaner methods, and authorities must collect waste and treat sewage properly. Citizens also have responsibilities: they should use bins, reduce plastic, save water and electricity, plant trees, and avoid burning rubbish. Environmental protection is not an occasional campaign. It is a daily practice shared by households, schools, businesses, and government. Clean surroundings support healthy lives and a safer future.

title: A Village Market Composition

plainContent: A lively centre of village trade A village market is more than a place to buy food. It is a meeting point where farmers, fishers, craftsmen, shopkeepers, and householders exchange goods and news. Usually it is held beside a road, canal, or river so that people from nearby villages can reach it easily. At dawn, vegetable sellers arrange baskets of pumpkins, gourds, rice, fish, and seasonal fruit. There are also stalls for clothes, tools, books, spices, and daily necessities. The busiest part is often the fish and meat section, while tea stalls give tired shoppers a place to rest. Sellers call out their prices, and buyers compare quality before bargaining politely. Such markets support the rural economy. Farmers receive money for their produce without travelling far, and villagers find necessary goods at reasonable prices. However, poor drainage, mud, litter, and overcrowding can make them unpleasant. A clean water supply, covered sheds, waste bins, and orderly lanes would improve them greatly. A well-managed village market therefore serves both commerce and community life. It connects producers with consumers and gives rural people a practical place to meet.

plainContent: Floods and life in Bangladesh Flooding is a regular natural event in Bangladesh because the country lies on the delta of several large rivers and receives heavy monsoon rain. Moderate floods can deposit fertile silt, but unusually deep or prolonged water causes widespread suffering. Homes, roads, schools, crops, livestock, and sanitation systems may be damaged. Families often move to embankments or shelters, while contaminated water increases the risk of diarrhoea and other diseases. Poor people lose work and possessions first and may struggle to rebuild. Preparation reduces loss. Authorities can maintain embankments, improve drainage, issue early warnings, stock emergency supplies, and keep shelters accessible. Families should protect documents, store clean water and dry food, learn evacuation routes, and avoid walking through fast or electrically contaminated water. Flood control must also respect natural waterways and wetlands. With careful planning, resilient housing, community cooperation, and prompt relief, Bangladesh can reduce the human cost of floods while benefiting from the fertile land that water sometimes renews.

title: The Season I Like Most Composition

plainContent: The Season I Like Most: Spring Bangladesh has six seasons, but spring is the one I enjoy most. It arrives after winter, usually during Falgun and Chaitra, when the weather becomes gentle rather than severely hot or cold. The air feels fresh, trees grow new leaves, and many flowers open across gardens and fields. Spring gives the countryside a cheerful appearance. Birds become active, bees visit blossoms, and people enjoy walking outdoors without the heavy rain of the monsoon or the strong heat of summer. Cultural programmes and the colours of Basanta Utsab add to the season’s happiness. Every season has value. Summer brings fruit, the rainy months support crops, autumn fills the sky with light, late autumn brings harvests, and winter offers cool mornings and vegetables. Yet spring feels especially balanced and lively. It refreshes both the landscape and the mind. The season is not free from storms or sudden heat, and climate change may alter its familiar pattern. We should protect trees and reduce pollution so that future generations can enjoy its flowers and mild beauty.

title: Mobile Phone paragraph

plainContent: Mobile Phone A mobile phone is a portable device used for calls, messages, photography, internet access, navigation, learning, and emergency assistance. Students can use educational applications, dictionaries, recorded lessons, and online libraries. Families can remain connected even when members live in different places. The device becomes harmful when it controls the user. Excessive gaming and social media can reduce sleep, attention, physical activity, and face-to-face conversation. Distracted driving, unsafe sharing of photographs, scams, and cyberbullying are additional risks. We should keep phones away during study and meals, protect personal information, and follow school and road rules. A phone is useful equipment when guided by self-control.

plainContent: Road Accidents A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, or roadside objects. It may occur on a highway, street, bridge, or village road. Speeding, reckless overtaking, driving while tired, using a phone, ignoring signals, and driving an unfit vehicle are common causes. Poor lighting, damaged roads, untrained drivers, and careless pedestrians add to the danger. Accidents cause death, injury, disability, emotional pain, and financial loss. A single crash can affect an entire family and delay traffic for thousands of people. Safety begins with behaviour: drivers should obey speed limits, wear seat belts or helmets, avoid alcohol and phones, and never drive when exhausted. Pedestrians should use footpaths and crossings where available and look carefully before crossing. Authorities must enforce licensing rules, inspect vehicles, repair roads, improve signs and lighting, and educate the public. Emergency services should be able to reach crash sites quickly. Road safety is a shared responsibility. Patience and respect for traffic rules can save lives that no later punishment can restore.

plainContent: A lesson in cautious listening A crow once found a piece of food and flew to a branch to eat it in peace. A fox noticed the prize and decided to obtain it without climbing the tree. The crow felt embarrassed, but it learned to judge praise carefully. Compliments can be sincere, yet they can also be a tool used by a selfish person. Moral: Think before acting when someone praises you for a hidden purpose.

title: Discipline Composition

plainContent: Discipline as a guide to life Discipline is the habit of following sensible rules and completing duties at the proper time. It does not mean blind punishment; it means controlling impulses so that an important goal is not lost to temporary comfort. A disciplined student attends lessons, keeps materials organized, studies regularly, respects others, and submits work honestly. A disciplined worker arrives on time and completes responsibilities carefully. In public life, obeying traffic rules, keeping promises, and protecting shared spaces are also forms of discipline. Without discipline, talent remains unreliable. A person may have intelligence but fail because of laziness, poor time management, or uncontrolled habits. Discipline turns small daily efforts into skill and achievement. It also builds self-respect because people learn that they can depend on their own decisions. Good routines should be realistic. Time for sleep, recreation, family, and rest prevents discipline from becoming unhealthy pressure. With patience and repeated practice, orderly habits make both personal and social life more successful.

The goat landed awkwardly, slipped into the ditch, and hurt its leg. It cried until a farmer heard the noise and helped it out. The animal had been attracted by the food and had not considered the obstacle. After recovering, it approached such places slowly, examined the ground, and looked for a safe crossing. The experience taught it a lasting lesson: excitement should not replace judgment. Before beginning a risky task, we should observe the situation, consider possible results, and choose a safe method.

title: Might is Right Completing Story
excerpt: Might is Right Completing Story: Dear learners, I wrote the three variants of this Completing Story on “Might is Right” […]
plainContent: Might Is Not Always Right A strong wolf often bullied the smaller animals near a forest stream. One day he claimed the drinking water belonged to him and threatened anyone who came near. The animals were afraid, but a clever hare suggested that they work together. They led the wolf toward a deep muddy pool by pretending that a larger rival had challenged him. The boastful wolf charged into the pool and became trapped. The animals then called the forest guard, who rescued the smaller creatures and took the wolf away from the stream. Strength without justice creates fear, not respect. The story reminds us that power should be controlled by wisdom and fairness, and that cooperation can protect the weak from an abuser.

title: My Favourite Game Composition
excerpt: My Favourite Game Composition: Dear students, here are three simple My Favourite Game Compositions in English. Read carefully and practice […]
plainContent: My Favourite Game Football is my favourite game. It is played by two teams that try to move a ball into the opponent’s goal while following the rules. The game requires speed, stamina, balance, accurate passing, and cooperation. A player cannot succeed alone; every member must understand a position and support the team. I enjoy playing football on the school field with friends in the afternoon. It keeps me fit and teaches me to remain alert, accept decisions, and continue trying after a mistake. Watching a good match is enjoyable too, but regular participation is more valuable. Players should warm up, use safe equipment, respect opponents, and show fair play. Football is recreation as well as a lesson in discipline and teamwork.

title: Student life Composition for Class 5, 6, 7, 8, SSC – Easy
excerpt: Student Life Composition: Students, here you will find an easy Student Life Essay/Composition with two variants. Learn its importance and […]
plainContent: Student Life Student life is the period when a person builds knowledge, habits, character, and plans for the future. It is not only a time for passing examinations. A student learns in classrooms, libraries, laboratories, playgrounds, families, and communities. The first duty of a student is sincere study. Regular attendance, careful reading, practice, and questions help turn information into understanding. Students should manage time, keep healthy routines, respect teachers, cooperate with classmates, and take part in useful cultural or sporting activities. Service projects can teach empathy and responsibility. Student life also has challenges. Competition, distraction, fear of failure, and pressure from others can cause stress. A balanced routine, honest communication, sufficient sleep, and asking for help can make these difficulties manageable. Success should be measured by progress and integrity, not only by marks. The habits formed during these years influence adult life. A disciplined, curious, kind, and adaptable learner can become a capable citizen. Therefore students should use their opportunities wisely and prepare themselves not just for employment, but for responsible participation in society.

title: Value of Time Composition for Class 6,7,8,SSC,HSC
excerpt: Value of Time Composition for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC: Hello learners! This short Value of Time Composition is written in […]
plainContent: The Value of Time Time is the portion of life in which every goal must be pursued. Money can sometimes be earned again and health may be restored with care, but a moment that has passed cannot be bought back. For that reason, wise people treat time as a resource more precious than possessions. Using time well does not mean working without rest. It means choosing priorities, beginning tasks promptly, and giving study, work, family, health, and relaxation their proper places. A student can divide a large assignment into daily steps and review progress each evening. A worker can prepare a short list and avoid unnecessary delays. Wasted hours often disappear through idleness, endless scrolling, or postponing difficult duties. Procrastination creates stress because unfinished work remains in the mind. Punctuality also shows respect for other people’s time and builds trust. We should set realistic goals, keep a routine, and adapt when unexpected events occur. Small useful actions repeated every day produce large results. When we value time, we make better use of education and opportunity and reduce regret about the past.

title: A Journey by Train Composition
excerpt: A Journey by Train Composition: Dear students, I have prepared this A Journey by Train Composition especially for you. Practice […]
plainContent: Watching the landscape from a carriage I recently travelled by train with my parents to visit relatives in another district. We reached the station with time to spare, checked the coach number, and settled beside a window. When the train began to move, the platform slowly disappeared and the journey found its steady rhythm. Outside, rice fields, ponds, bridges, villages, and lines of trees passed like scenes in a changing picture. At larger stations vendors offered tea, fruit, and snacks. We shared our food, talked with a family in the next seats, and listened to the regular sound of the wheels. The railway made the trip comfortable because we could move about without watching the road. We arrived in the afternoon after a short delay. The journey taught me that travel is not only about reaching a destination; observing people and places along the way can make the experience memorable.

title: A Village Fair Composition
excerpt: A Village Fair Composition or Class 6, 7, 8, SSC, and HSC: Dear learners, I have written this A Village […]
plainContent: A seasonal gathering in the countryside A village fair is a temporary event where people from nearby communities meet to trade, enjoy entertainment, and spend a festive day together. It is often held beside a river, on an open field, or near a shrine during a cultural or religious occasion. Families arrive in groups, and the usually quiet area becomes lively. Stalls may sell pottery, bamboo work, cloth, toys, books, sweets, spices, and farm products. Children enjoy rides, puppet shows, magic, or music, while adults compare goods and meet friends. The fair gives local craftspeople a chance to reach customers and can strengthen small rural businesses. A fair also needs responsible management. Clean drinking water, toilets, waste bins, first aid, safe rides, and security are essential. Gambling, pickpocketing, overcrowding, and plastic waste can spoil the event. With proper supervision, a village fair offers recreation, preserves local crafts, and brings people together in a shared community experience.

title: Money Can’t Bring Happiness Completing Story
excerpt: Money Cannot Bring Happiness Story: Write and complete the story “Money Cannot Bring Happiness” in simple English. Useful for Class […]
plainContent: Money Cannot Bring Happiness A wealthy merchant lived in a large house but was always anxious about losing his possessions. He rarely spoke kindly to anyone and had no time for friends. One day a flood damaged his store. Although he still had enough money to rebuild, he felt alone and miserable. A poor neighbor who had often received the merchant’s small acts of help brought food and gathered other villagers to repair the house. Their care touched the merchant. He began sharing his wealth, spending time with people, and helping local children study. His life became peaceful. Money can provide comfort and meet necessities, but affection, health, trust, and meaningful relationships give life its deeper happiness.

title: Physical Exercise Composition
excerpt: Physical Exercise Composition for Classes 6,7,8,9,10, SSC with 250, 300 Words: Here you will find a short and easy Physical […]
plainContent: Physical Exercise Physical exercise means purposeful movement that strengthens the body and supports mental well-being. Walking, jogging, swimming, cycling, stretching, games, and sports are all useful forms. The right activity depends on a person’s age, health, and ability; a gentle walk may suit an older person, while a healthy young person may enjoy running or team sports. Regular activity improves circulation, muscle strength, balance, sleep, and concentration. It can help prevent obesity and several lifestyle-related illnesses. Exercise also reduces stress because movement gives the mind a break from study and work. It need not require expensive equipment. A brisk walk in a safe place, simple stretching, or playing football with friends can be enough to begin. Exercise should be taken gradually. People should warm up, drink adequate water, wear suitable clothing, and rest when they feel pain or dizziness. Someone with a medical condition should seek professional advice before starting a demanding routine. Exercise cannot replace nutritious food, sleep, hygiene, or medical care, but it works with them to build a healthy life. A regular, enjoyable habit is better than an occasional burst of exhausting effort.

title: Population Problem in Bangladesh Composition
excerpt: Population Problem in Bangladesh Composition: In this lesson, you will find a simple Population Problem in Bangladesh Composition. Practice it […]
plainContent: Population Problem in Bangladesh Bangladesh has a large population living on limited land. A population becomes a problem when people increase faster than jobs, housing, education, health care, food, transport, and natural resources can support them. Crowded cities, pressure on farmland, unemployment, pollution, and shortages of public services are connected to this challenge. The causes include early marriage, limited awareness of family planning, poverty, and unequal access to education. When families cannot provide adequate nutrition or schooling for every child, poverty may continue from one generation to the next. Rapid urban growth also creates unplanned settlements and traffic congestion. The solution is not to blame poor families. Girls’ education, health services, informed reproductive choices, and opportunities for women can help families plan responsibly. The country must also create productive work through agriculture, industry, technology, and vocational training. Better urban planning, efficient public transport, and protection of farmland are equally important. Population can become a strength when citizens are educated, healthy, and employed. Government agencies, schools, families, and communities must work together so that Bangladesh’s people are supported by resources and can contribute fully to national development.

title: My Family, Our Family, Your Family paragraph
excerpt: My Family paragraph: Dear learners, here is an easy paragraph on My Family. Read it gently, feel the meaning, and […]
plainContent: My Family My family is a small, caring group. We share a home where everyone has responsibilities and tries to support the others. My parents work hard and encourage us to be honest, respectful, and diligent. The children attend school, help with simple household tasks, and learn to cooperate rather than quarrel. We eat together whenever possible and discuss the day’s events. On holidays we visit relatives, prepare special food, or enjoy a short outing. When someone is ill or worried, the rest of the family offers practical help and affection. We may not agree about everything, but we listen and forgive one another. My family gives me security, teaches me good habits, and inspires me to become a useful person.

title: My Mother paragraph for Class 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 and SSC
excerpt: My Mother paragraph for Class 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 & SSC: Beloved students, here is a heartfelt paragraph on My Mother. Read it […]
plainContent: My Mother My mother is one of the most important people in my life. She manages many responsibilities with patience and still finds time to listen to us. She encourages me to study honestly, speak politely, keep my room tidy, and help people who need support. When I make a mistake, she corrects me firmly but kindly. She prepares our meals, cares for the family, and often puts her own comfort aside for us. I admire her practical wisdom, courage, and sympathy. She also reminds me that good character matters more than high marks or wealth. I try to show my gratitude by respecting her advice, sharing household work, and working hard. Her love gives our home warmth and gives me confidence to face difficulties.

title: Myself paragraph for Primary and High School
excerpt: Myself paragraph: Hello, my dear students, this is a short paragraph about Myself. Read carefully, understand the style, and use […]
plainContent: Myself My name is Samiya, and I am a student in Class Six. I live with my parents and younger brother in a friendly neighborhood. My school begins in the morning and offers lessons in Bangla, English, mathematics, science, social studies, and religion. I enjoy English and science because they help me understand people and the world around me. I try to attend school regularly, finish my work, and treat classmates kindly. In my free time I read storybooks, play outdoor games, and help my family. I hope to become a doctor one day so that I can serve people who cannot easily afford treatment. I know that this dream will require steady study, good health, honesty, and perseverance.

title: Water Pollution paragraph
excerpt: Water Pollution paragraph: Dear students, this short paragraph on Water Pollution is written just for you. Read it slowly, understand […]
plainContent: Water Pollution Water pollution occurs when harmful substances enter rivers, ponds, lakes, groundwater, or the sea and make the water unsafe. People, animals, and plants all need clean water, so pollution threatens health and the balance of nature. Factories may release untreated chemicals, while households often add sewage, plastic, detergent, and other waste. Farmers’ fertilisers and pesticides can wash into streams. Boats sometimes spill oil or throw rubbish overboard. Polluted water may carry disease, kill fish, damage crops, and reduce the supply of safe drinking water. Prevention begins with responsible behaviour. Homes and factories should treat wastewater before releasing it, and rubbish must be collected instead of dumped into drains or rivers. Farmers can use chemicals carefully and protect waterways with vegetation. Boats, markets, and industries need regular inspection. Authorities should enforce environmental laws and provide affordable waste services. Citizens can help by reducing plastic, using bins, joining clean-up activities, and reporting illegal dumping. Rivers and ponds belong to the whole community. Protecting them today safeguards public health, food, wildlife, and future generations.

title: Dengue Fever paragraph for Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC
excerpt: Dengue Fever paragraph: Hello students, in this lesson, you will find a clear and simple paragraph on Dengue Fever with […]
plainContent: Dengue fever and prevention Dengue is a viral illness spread mainly by infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes often breed in small amounts of water collected in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters, or uncovered tanks. A patient may develop sudden fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea, or a rash. Anyone with these symptoms should contact a qualified health professional, especially if the fever is high or persistent. Bleeding, repeated vomiting, abdominal pain, unusual sleepiness, or difficulty breathing are warning signs that require urgent care. Self-medication can be risky, so advice from a doctor is important. Families can reduce risk by emptying containers, cleaning drains, covering stored water, wearing protective clothing, and using approved mosquito protection. Schools and local authorities should keep public areas clean and spread accurate information. Community action is the strongest defence against dengue.

title: Childhood Memories Composition
excerpt: Childhood Memories composition: Hello students, in this lesson, you will find a composition on Childhood Memories. Practice three different versions […]
plainContent: Memories that shaped my early years Childhood remains a bright chapter in my memory because ordinary events felt like adventures. I grew up in a neighbourhood where homes stood close to a pond and a wide field. Every afternoon, friends gathered there for football, hide-and-seek, or races among the trees. My grandmother added warmth to those years. She told us folk tales after dinner and taught us to respect guests, animals, and older people. On rainy days, we watched the water fill the courtyard and made paper boats. During holidays, cousins visited, and the house became noisy with games, arguments, and laughter. School also gave my childhood a strong foundation. A patient teacher encouraged me to read beyond the textbook. I still remember the pride I felt when I completed my first storybook. The lessons learned from friends, family, play, and school gradually shaped my character more than any single event. Growing older brings new duties, but childhood memories remain a source of courage. They remind me that happiness can be found in friendship, imagination, and kindness rather than in expensive possessions.

title: Duties of a Student Composition
excerpt: Duties of a Student Composition for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC, HSC: Hello, beautiful students, here is a very important […]
plainContent: Responsibilities of a student A student’s first responsibility is to learn sincerely. This means attending classes, listening carefully, completing assignments, reading beyond the lesson when possible, and asking questions without embarrassment. Regular revision is more valuable than hurried study before an examination. Students also owe duties to their families and society. They should respect parents and teachers, behave courteously with classmates, keep promises, and help younger or weaker learners. Honesty in examinations and assignments is essential because education loses its value when marks are obtained through deception. Good students care for their health through sleep, nutritious food, cleanliness, and exercise. They use leisure constructively and avoid habits that damage concentration. They should protect school property, keep the campus clean, obey reasonable rules, and take part in useful social or cultural activities. A student is preparing not only for a job but for citizenship. Knowledge joined with character, responsibility, and compassion enables young people to contribute to their families and country.

title: My Favourite Hobby Composition
excerpt: My Favourite Hobby composition: Hello students! In this lesson, you will find two versions of “My Favourite Hobby Composition.” Simple […]
plainContent: My Favourite Hobby Reading is my favourite hobby. I enjoy storybooks, biographies, travel writing, and simple science books. Reading introduces me to places and people I may never meet and encourages me to imagine different possibilities. It also improves vocabulary, spelling, concentration, and general knowledge. I keep a small reading schedule instead of waiting for a holiday. After finishing a book, I note its main idea and discuss interesting parts with friends. I choose books carefully and balance fiction with informative writing. Reading is inexpensive when we use a school or public library. It gives quiet pleasure, helps me express ideas clearly, and makes free time more meaningful.

title: Newspaper Composition
excerpt: Newspaper composition: Dear learners, here is a three-composition on the Newspaper. Read carefully and practice it well to prepare for […]
plainContent: Newspaper A newspaper is a regular publication that reports events and presents comment on matters of public interest. It may appear in print, on a website, or through a digital app. Its pages commonly include national and international news, education, science, health, business, sports, culture, weather, and classified notices. Newspapers connect citizens with the country and the wider world. A student who reads one regularly learns new words, discovers useful facts, and develops ideas for essays and discussions. Reports about public decisions can also help people understand their rights and responsibilities. Editorials and columns encourage readers to think about problems from different perspectives. A newspaper must be read thoughtfully. A responsible reader checks the source, notices the date, and does not share an unverified claim simply because its headline is exciting. News and opinion should not be confused. Printed papers remain useful, while digital editions make information faster to access. Newspapers can influence society by exposing wrongdoing, highlighting neglected communities, and encouraging constructive debate. Their value is greatest when journalists work honestly and readers remain critical. Therefore, regular newspaper reading is a simple way to become informed, improve language skill, and participate wisely in civic life.

title: Students and Social Services Composition
excerpt: Students and Social Services composition: My dear students, here is an easy composition on Students and Social Services. Learn it […]
plainContent: Students and Social Services Students are learners, but they are also members of their communities. Alongside gaining knowledge, they can contribute time and energy to social welfare in ways that do not harm their studies. Service teaches cooperation, sympathy, leadership, and practical responsibility. Students may organise a cleanliness campaign, plant and care for trees, help younger children read, collect books for a community library, or explain safe hygiene and disaster preparedness. During floods or storms they can assist an approved relief group by sorting supplies, raising awareness, or distributing information under adult supervision. They should never enter dangerous water or handle medical work without trained guidance. The first duty remains education. A student who studies seriously develops the skills needed for larger service later. Schools can create clubs, volunteering schedules, and projects with local organisations so that participation is safe and fair. Service must respect the dignity and privacy of the people receiving help; it should not become a performance for praise. When young people combine learning with compassion, communities become stronger. Small, regular acts of responsibility can prepare students to become thoughtful citizens and future leaders.

title: Wonders of Modern Science Composition
excerpt: Wonders of Modern Science composition: My dear students, today you will learn an easy composition on Wonders of Modern Science. […]
plainContent: Wonders of Modern Science Science has transformed how people live, work, travel, communicate, and protect health. Electricity lights homes and powers machines, hospitals, schools, and factories. Telephones and the internet allow people on different continents to exchange information within seconds. Computers help us learn, design, calculate, store records, and solve complex problems. Modern transport takes passengers and goods across land, sea, and air. Satellites support weather forecasts, navigation, communication, and disaster observation. In medicine, microscopes, vaccines, imaging, surgery, and laboratory tests help diagnose and treat disease. Radio and television bring education, news, and entertainment to large audiences. Agricultural technology can improve irrigation, seed quality, and food production. Science also has risks. Pollution, weapons, unsafe technology, excessive screen use, and the misuse of personal data can harm society. Scientific knowledge must therefore be guided by ethics, safety, and concern for the environment. Technology is not automatically a blessing; its effect depends on how people design and use it. When knowledge is applied responsibly, science can reduce suffering and expand opportunity. Students should learn not only scientific facts but also the judgment needed to use them for peace, health, and sustainable progress.

title: Aim in Life Composition
excerpt: Aim in Life composition for Class 6,7,8, SSC, and HSC: Dear students, here is a simple composition on Aim in […]
plainContent: Choosing a direction A person’s aim in life is a clear idea about the kind of work and contribution he or she hopes to make. Without a direction, time and talent can easily be wasted. My present aim is to become a teacher who makes learning accessible to children in both towns and villages. I have chosen this goal because education changes the opportunities available to families. A capable teacher can explain lessons, encourage shy learners, and help students develop honesty, discipline, and independent judgment. To prepare, I must study regularly, improve my communication skills, read widely, and learn how to use modern teaching tools. Patience and empathy are as important as examination results. An aim should guide daily habits rather than remain an attractive sentence. I will review my progress, correct weaknesses, and seek advice from experienced people. Whatever profession a person chooses, success is most meaningful when personal achievement is joined with useful service to society.

title: Industry is the Key to Success Completing Story
excerpt: Industry is the Key to Success Completing Story: Are you looking for Industry is the Key to Success Completing Story? […]
plainContent: Industry Is the Key to Success Two classmates prepared for an important examination. Arif studied only on the night before each test and hoped luck would help him. His friend Nabil made a practical plan, reviewed a small section each day, asked questions, and corrected his mistakes. At first Arif laughed at Nabil’s steady routine. When the examination arrived, however, Nabil remembered the lessons calmly, while Arif found that hurried reading had left him confused. Nabil earned an excellent result through continuous effort. Arif understood that talent and wishes are not enough without work. From then on, he began studying regularly and improved. The story shows that perseverance turns ability into achievement; patient industry is more dependable than last-minute excitement.

title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin Completing Story
excerpt: The Pied Piper of Hamelin Completing Story: Complete the famous story of The Pied Piper of Hamelin in simple English. […]
plainContent: The Pied Piper of Hamelin The town of Hamelin was overrun by rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people. The mayor promised a large reward to anyone who could rid the town of the pests. A travelling piper arrived and said that his music could lead the rats away. He played a strange, bright tune, and every rat followed him through the streets and out to the river. He guided them safely away, then returned to claim the promised payment. The mayor had expected the piper to work for less and refused to pay the full reward. The piper warned him that a promise made publicly must be honoured, but the mayor dismissed him. The piper then played another tune. This time the town’s children followed him beyond the gates. When the mayor and citizens realised what was happening, they begged him to return them. The piper brought the children back only after the town paid what it had promised and apologised. From then on, Hamelin’s leaders kept their word. Moral: A promise is a responsibility, not an opportunity for dishonest bargaining.

title: Wisdom of King Solomon Completing Story for Class 6-10, HSC
excerpt: Wisdom of King Solomon Completing Story: Complete the story of King Solomon’s wisdom in easy English. The Wisdom of King […]
plainContent: The Wisdom of King Solomon The Queen of Sheba once visited King Solomon to test the wisdom for which he was famous. Among her gifts were two garlands that looked exactly alike. One was made from fresh roses; the other was artificial. She placed them before the king and asked him to identify the natural one. Solomon did not touch either garland. Instead, he opened the windows of the room and waited. Bees soon entered, attracted by the scent of the living flowers. They settled on one garland, while the other remained untouched. Solomon pointed to the flowers visited by the bees and gave his answer. The Queen of Sheba admired his careful observation. He had solved the problem not by guessing, but by finding a simple test based on the natural difference between the two objects. The story teaches that wisdom includes patience, attention, and the ability to use evidence. When a problem seems confusing, we should avoid rushing to a conclusion. A calm mind can often discover a practical clue that is hidden in plain sight.

title: Global Warming Paragraph
excerpt: Global Warming Paragraph for Class 6, 7, 8, HSC, SSC: Write and learn a short paragraph on Global Warming in […]
plainContent: Global Warming Global warming means the long-term rise in Earth’s average temperature. Burning coal, oil, and gas releases greenhouse gases that hold extra heat in the atmosphere. Cutting forests makes the problem worse because trees absorb carbon dioxide. Hotter weather can melt ice, raise sea levels, intensify storms, and harm crops, animals, and human health. The solution requires action from governments, industries, and individuals. Clean energy, efficient transport, energy-saving buildings, tree planting, and responsible consumption can reduce emissions. People should avoid waste and support policies that protect nature. Because pollution crosses national borders, countries must cooperate. Early action is less costly and more effective than waiting for damage to become irreversible.

title: Illiteracy Problem in Bangladesh Dialogue for all Class

plainContent: A Conversation About Illiteracy in Bangladesh Rafi: Our village still has many adults who cannot read or write. Nadia: That is a serious obstacle. Without literacy, people may struggle to read medicine labels, understand official notices, or manage money. Rafi: Poverty, distance from schools, and early employment keep many children away from education. Nadia: Families also need to understand that schooling is an investment, not a waste of time. Rafi: What can communities do? Nadia: They can support free evening classes, prevent child marriage and child labor, and encourage parents to send every child to school. Teachers, local leaders, charities, and the government must work together. Rafi: Then literacy will improve both personal opportunity and national development. Nadia: Exactly. An educated population can make informed decisions and contribute more effectively to society.

title: Dialogue Merits and Demerits of Mobile Phones for Class 6-12
excerpt: Dialogue Merits and Demerits of Mobile Phones: Learn a Dialogue on the Merits and Demerits of Using Mobile Phones. Easy […]
plainContent: Using a mobile phone wisely Mahi: Mobile phones are useful, but many students cannot put them down. Are they more harmful than helpful? Ritu: Their value depends on use. A phone can connect families, provide maps, emergency help, educational lessons, and quick communication. Mahi: What are the dangers? Ritu: Distraction, poor sleep, excessive gaming, misleading information, privacy loss, and online harassment. Looking at a screen while walking or crossing a road is dangerous too. Mahi: How can students keep a balance? Ritu: Set periods for study and rest, silence unnecessary notifications, keep the phone away during class, and avoid it before sleeping. Check privacy settings and never share another person’s picture without permission. Mahi: So the device should serve our plans rather than control our attention. Ritu: Exactly. A useful tool becomes harmful when it replaces study, exercise, face-to-face conversation, or sleep.

title: Dialogue Preparation for Upcoming Exam for Class 6,7,8, SSC
excerpt: Dialogue Preparation for Upcoming Exam: Practice a Dialogue about Preparation for Upcoming Exam. Simple and exam-focused conversation for school and […]
plainContent: Preparing calmly for an examination Fahim: Our examination starts next month. I am anxious because several chapters remain unfinished. Rony: Make a list of the syllabus today. Mark what you know, what needs revision, and what requires help from a teacher. Fahim: Should I spend the first week reading everything? Rony: Combine learning with practice. After studying a chapter, close the book and answer questions without looking. Keep a notebook of mistakes for later review. Fahim: I often waste time on my phone. Rony: Study in focused periods, silence notifications, and place the phone outside the room. Take short breaks, sleep properly, and eat regular meals. Fahim: How should I use the final days? Rony: Revise summaries and practise full papers under time limits. Do not begin an unfamiliar large topic at midnight before the test. Fahim: I will follow a steady plan and ask for help instead of hiding my confusion. Rony: That is the best preparation: organized work, honest self-assessment, and a rested mind.

title: Dividing the Bread Completing story for Class 6-9, HSC
excerpt: Dividing the Bread completing story. In some books, this story mentions the mouse/rat and the monkey, while in others it […]
plainContent: Two quarrelling friends and a clever monkey Two young villagers found a round loaf on the road. Both claimed to have seen it first, and neither would agree to share it fairly. Their argument grew louder until a monkey sitting in a nearby tree offered to divide the bread for them. The monkey broke the loaf into two pieces, but one looked slightly larger. He bit the larger piece to make the halves equal. Now the other piece appeared larger, so he took a bite from that one too. Each bite made the loaf smaller, while the monkey continued to announce that he was only correcting the difference. The friends finally understood what was happening. They apologized to each other and asked for the remaining bread, but the monkey swallowed the last crumbs and ran away. Their quarrel had cost them the whole meal. Had they divided the bread honestly at the beginning, both would have eaten. The story teaches that unnecessary disputes can allow a third party to profit from our foolishness.

title: Dialogue Bad Effect of Smoking

plainContent: A warning about tobacco Rafi: My older cousin has started smoking because he thinks it makes him look mature. Joya: Tobacco does not prove maturity. It contains addictive substances and exposes the body to harmful chemicals. Rafi: What damage can it cause? Joya: It raises the risk of lung disease, heart problems, stroke, and several cancers. Smoke also harms people nearby, especially children. Money spent on cigarettes could support food, books, or savings. Rafi: Some people say they can stop whenever they wish. Joya: Dependence makes quitting difficult, but support from a doctor, family, or cessation programme can help. Avoiding triggers and replacing the habit with exercise or another activity is useful. Rafi: We should not tease someone who is trying to quit. Joya: Right. Encouragement is more helpful than shame. Young people should learn the facts before advertising or peer pressure influences them. Rafi: I will share reliable health information with my cousin and ask whether he wants help.

title: Food Adulteration paragraph for Class 6,7,8, HSC, SSC
excerpt: Food Adulteration paragraph for Class 6,7,8, HSC, SSC: Food Adulteration paragraph written for all classes. We write in a different […]
plainContent: The danger of adulterated food Food adulteration occurs when sellers mix inferior, contaminated, or harmful substances into food or use unsafe chemicals to make it look better or last longer. Milk, spices, oil, fruit, fish, sweets, and packaged products can all be affected. Eating such food may cause immediate stomach problems and can damage organs after repeated exposure. Children, older people, and those with weak health face particular risks. Adulteration is therefore not a minor business offence; it threatens public health. Consumers should buy from reliable sources, inspect packaging, check dates, wash produce, and be cautious about unnatural colours or unusually low prices. Authorities must test food, inspect businesses, punish offenders, and educate the public. Honest sellers and informed buyers can help create a safer food market.

title: Drug Addiction Paragraph for Class 6-12, SSC, HSC
excerpt: Drug Addiction Paragraph for class 6,7,8, SSC, and HSC learners. Five variants are written this post with two images. So […]
plainContent: Protecting young people from drugs Drug addiction begins when repeated use of a substance changes a person’s body and behaviour. What starts as curiosity or pressure from friends can become dependence. An addicted person may lose interest in study, work, health, and family responsibilities. The effects include illness, financial hardship, broken relationships, accidents, and crime. A family should not hide the problem or wait until it becomes severe. Doctors, counsellors, and treatment centres can provide safer and more effective help. Education, sports, creative activities, caring relationships, and honest conversations can prevent many young people from experimenting. Authorities must stop illegal trafficking while making treatment available to those who need it. We should reject drugs firmly but treat affected people with humanity so that they can seek recovery.

title: A Day Labourer paragraph for class 6,7,8, SSC & HSC
excerpt: A Day Labourer paragraph for class 6, class 7, class 8, class 9, class 10, SSC, and HSC with 150, […]
plainContent: The dignity of daily work A day labourer earns a living by working wherever labour is available. He may carry bricks, dig soil, harvest crops, repair roads, or assist builders. Usually he has no permanent employer, so each morning he goes to a common meeting place and waits to be hired. His work is physically demanding and his income is uncertain. Rain, illness, or a shortage of construction projects can leave his family without enough money. Even so, an honest labourer rises early, works patiently, and supports relatives through his effort. His hands help build houses, roads, schools, and markets used by everyone. Society should respect this work and ensure fair wages, safe conditions, clean water, and medical support. We can also help by paying promptly and treating labourers politely. Their lives remind us that every lawful occupation deserves dignity and that progress depends on people whose work is often overlooked.

title: An Ant and a Dove Completing Story For Class 6-10, HSC
excerpt: An Ant and a Dove Completing Story For Class 6, 7, 8, SSC, HSC students. Today I’m going to share […]
plainContent: Help returned at the right moment An ant slipped into a stream while searching for water. The current carried it away, and it struggled to reach the bank. A dove noticed the danger, dropped a leaf beside the ant, and gave it a floating platform. The ant climbed onto the leaf and survived. A few days later the ant saw a hunter taking aim at the dove. It hurried to the hunter and bit his ankle. The sudden pain made him miss, and the dove flew into the trees. Neither creature had expected payment when helping the other; each simply acted when a life was in danger. The story shows that a small act may become important later. Strength and size are not the only ways to help someone. Compassion builds a world in which even the weakest can protect another. Moral: Do good whenever you can; kindness often returns unexpectedly.

title: Dialogue Aim in Life – For Class 6,7,8, SSC, HSC

plainContent: Talking about future goals Imran: Have you chosen the career you want to pursue? Hasan: I hope to become a civil engineer. I want to design safe bridges and roads for communities that remain poorly connected. Imran: Why does that interest you? Hasan: I enjoy mathematics, drawing, and solving practical problems. More importantly, useful infrastructure can improve education, trade, and emergency services. Imran: I am interested in medicine. A doctor needs scientific knowledge, patience, and compassion, so I know that the path will require years of disciplined study. Hasan: A goal is helpful only when it becomes a plan. I am strengthening my mathematics and science, reading about engineering, and learning to work carefully. Imran: I am doing something similar: following a study timetable and volunteering at a community clinic when possible. Hasan: Whatever career we choose, honesty and service should guide our work. A profession is not valuable merely because it earns money. Imran: Exactly. Clear aims give direction, but good character determines how we use our skills.

title: Dialogue Physical Exercise: for Class 6, 7, 8, 9-10, 11-12
